proposed_claim_rows.label: Finite-prime weighted support irrationality
proposed_claim_rows.statement: For every integer base b >= 2, every infinite positive support A with finite weighted mass for some finite nonempty prime set P has irrational support series. If a host H has finite base-two weighted mass, then every infinite subset A of H has irrational support series at every integer base b >= 2. This is a sufficient support criterion, not the universal statement.

proposed_claim_rows.label: Strengthened positive-cover support irrationality
proposed_claim_rows.statement: A strengthened positive divisor-cover datum with summable scaled cost makes every infinite subset of its host irrational at every integer base b >= 2. The statement retains the nonlinear cover majorant and summability hypotheses; it does not cover arbitrary supports.

proposed_claim_rows.label: Mixed weighted and positive-cover support irrationality
proposed_claim_rows.statement: Let E have finite base-two finite-prime weighted mass and let V lie in a strengthened positive-cover host. Every infinite support A contained in E union V has irrational support series at every integer base b >= 2. The theorem uses a common observation scale; it does not assume separate irrationality conclusions for the two components.

proposed_claim_rows.label: Reciprocal-summable support irrationality at every integer base
proposed_claim_rows.statement: For every integer base b >= 2 and every infinite support A, summability of the reciprocal-support mass implies that the support series is irrational. No pairwise-coprimality hypothesis is required.
